newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products sharply higher on soy, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products sharply higher on soy, weather.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures were sharply higher at midsession Monday, with the markets pulled up by limit gains in soybeans, traders said.
CBOT August soybeans were up the 30-cent-per-bushel limit in response to a hot, dry weekend in much of the U.S. Midwest.
The weather is generating concern about the development of the soybean crop, especially in overly dry areas like central Illinois, traders said.
August soyoil rallied the 1.00 cent a lb daily limit and August soymeal rallied the $10.00 per ton daily limit near the market's open as well.
The run-up in CBOT soymeal prices was keeping buyers out of U.S. cash markets and basis values were mostly unchanged, dealers said.
In early soymeal trade, ING bought 200 lots December, Refco bought 200 lots August and Rosenthal sold 100 lots August, floor sources said.
In soyoil, Cargill sold 200 lots August, 100 September and 200 December.
At 1126 CDT, August soymeal was up $8.20 a ton at $253.80, and other months were up $7.00 to $8.80. August soyoil was up 0.57 cent a lb at 22.50 cents and others were up 0.42 to 0.74.
